title: SSP-5.0 — Public Work And Series Metadata Sanity Note
summary: confirm the bounded fit, owners, risks, evidence and stop conditions for exact published-document URL projection into Work and Series payloads
content_html:
SSP-5.0 — Public Work And Series Metadata Sanity Note

Outcome

SSP-5 fits the current architecture as a bounded derived-public-data delivery. The final public-eligible canonical document source supplies an optional normalized Work or Series subject, the existing public document-location projection supplies its URL, and the existing Work/Series by-ID generator owns the enriched public payload. These inputs must be joined by exact document identity. No canonical Catalogue association, browser lookup, title or URL inference, or separate complete-public-document-inventory file is required.

The gate is complete. SSP-5.1 may begin only after explicit implementation approval; no runtime behavior, generated Catalogue payload, or public presentation changes at SSP-5.0.

Confirmed Owners And Fit

  • SSP-1 remains the sole subject-normalization authority. A valid Work or Series result contributes one exact typed target; none, Folder, malformed, and conflicting results remain non-blocking and contribute no Catalogue document URL.
  • Docs publication remains the public-eligibility authority. SSP-5 consumes only the final successful public set, so viewable is next-Publish eligibility rather than proof that a document is currently public.
  • The existing document-location projection remains the public URL authority. The projection already holds exact document identity while it is built even though the emitted public location records do not expose that identity.
  • Existing Work and Series by-ID generation remains the only public payload writer. Canonical works.json and series.json, authored links, aggregate search products, media generation, and route presentation remain outside this delivery.
  • The successful Docs Publish boundary owns follow-through. Derived failure must not roll back, repeat, or change the initiating publication mutation, and the last complete Catalogue payload must remain available.

The current Analysis Works sources provide a representative boundary: a public Series-subject document is present in the public document set, while a non-viewable Work-subject document is absent. Focused implementation evidence can exercise this distinction without making Analysis lifecycle or collection membership an association rule.

Blast Radius And Deliverables

The broad blast radius covers configured public parent and sub-scope document sources, the exact public-location builder, Work and Series payload composition and payload-version calculation, cleanup or deletion paths that finalize those payloads, successful Publish follow-through, and focused generated-data tests. It does not include public Work or Series page presentation.

SSP-5 must produce deterministic URL-string doc_url[] arrays for zero or more public documents on every exact Work and Series by-ID payload. Work subjects affect only their exact Work, Series subjects affect only their exact Series, and membership produces neither Work-to-Series roll-up nor Series-to-Work fan-out. Documents with no usable Work or Series subject remain ordinarily published and absent from both reverse lookups. Non-viewable, unpublished, deleted, and reassigned documents must not remain in the result.

Publish, unpublish, deletion, and subject reassignment must update only the exact affected old and new Work or Series payloads after publication succeeds. Payload hashes and versions must cover the complete enriched output, and every normal generation or cleanup path must preserve the same doc_url[] contract.

Implementation Risks And Required Evidence

  • Public document-location records omit doc_id, and the current location producer supports only a bounded set of public scopes. Implementation must preserve exact identity inside the existing projection seam and cover every configured public collection that can contribute. It must not parse a URL, title, filename, or route to recover identity, silently narrow SSP-5 to Analysis, or invent another public inventory.
  • The normal scoped Catalogue build also rebuilds products outside SSP-5. Follow-through therefore needs a narrow reuse of the existing by-ID payload writer rather than a broad aggregate, search, semantic, or media rebuild and rather than a second Catalogue engine.
  • An unpublish, deletion, or reassignment can remove the source that identified the old target. Implementation must obtain exact old and new affected targets from complete desired-versus-current projection evidence or another bounded exact seam. It must stop before adding a persistent lineage table, generic relationship registry, or inferred fallback.
  • Work and Series payload versioning and cleanup paths currently assume their existing shapes. Focused tests must prove normal generation, zero and many URLs, deterministic ordering, removal, reassignment, targeted writes, version changes, and retention of prior complete payloads on derived failure.
  • Public-isolation evidence must prove that Manage associations, local paths, invalid-subject evidence, Project State, Semantic Token usage, non-viewable sources, and browser presentation do not enter the payload or trigger the projection.

Boundary And Stop Condition

SSP-5.1 must stop for review if implementation requires canonical Catalogue records to own document associations, changes publication eligibility, reads private association or semantic-usage products, exposes Manage-only subject data in the public location schema merely to perform the join, introduces a general inventory or relationship service, rebuilds unrelated Catalogue products, couples publication to retry or rollback, infers identity, expands related subjects, or adds a public route consumer.

The proposed implementation remains bounded only while it reuses the exact Docs publication/location and Catalogue by-ID generation owners, adds the doc_url[] projection and payload-version coverage, and limits post-success follow-through to exact affected payloads. Public display remains a separate later Catalogue delivery outside Sub-Scope Publishing.
